newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Argyle sale opens with three carat diamond.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Argyle sale opens with three carat diamond.

text.p: Argyle Diamonds, the world's biggest-volume diamond mine, on Friday opened its annual Pink Diamond Tender, which this year features the largest polished pink diamond the company has ever offered for sale.

Centrepiece of the tender is a 3.66 carat cushion cut gem, one of two diamonds in the collection weighing over three carats. The collection comprises 47 polished diamonds weighing a total of 47.82 carats.
Argyle managing director Gordon Gilchrist described the collection as the most valuable diamonds produced by the mine this year.

Argyle officials told reporters the value of diamonds in its tender was confidential but a document released by the company showed that last year's collection sold for over US$4.5 million at an average price of over US$100,000 per carat.
Sales manager David Fardon told reporters over 500 diamonds had been offered since the tender was launched in 1985.
"Only six other three carat-plus diamonds have been presented out of that total," Fardon said.
This year's collection has previously been offered in Hong Kong and Tokyo and will move to London for two days from September 19 and then to Geneva on September 26.
Pink diamonds form less than 0.1 per cent of Argyle's annual output of about 35 million carats.
Argyle Diamonds is owned about 60 percent by RTZ-CRA and about 40 percent by Ashton Mining Ltd.
